I was asked recently by a new person at our local Uke club if I had any advise that I could offer them that has worked for me. So I made a list of some things that have helped me, with a brief explanation, note or example of each.

  1. Frequency is better than duration. Practice every day even if it's only for five minutes. Pick the instrument up as often as you can throughout the day. Keep it where you are. Walk around with it, hold it while you are relaxing. It will become a part of you and your daily life.

  2. Focus on the mistakes but don't practice them. Don't practice a piece from the start each time you make a mistake, isolate the mistake and practice just that part until you have improved it to where you are happy with it. That way you are not practicing 'making the mistake'.

  3. Don't compare yourself to others. Everyone's journey is different. Be inspired by your own progress with the instrument. Each day you are more skilled than the day before. Keep a diary and you will see your journey more clearly.

  4. Practice well. Make everything you do while practicing the best that you can. Think about what you are doing and what you are trying to achieve. Record your practice in your diary and on your phone. Make notes in your diary about things you need to practice as they come to you so you don't waste your precious practice time thinking of things to do.

  5. Slowly is the fastest way to improve. Move slowly and focus carefully on your movements. Listen intensely to the sounds that you make with your instrument. Make each movement as efficient and each sound as beautiful as it can be. Strum so that every string can be heard separately as well as part of the overall movement, don't rush from the top string to the bottom, enjoy the journey

  6. Finish on a high. The most important thing of all is your attitude. Never end a session with the instrument feeling bad, end your session with the instrument feeling great. A great experience is remembered and desired.
